topups.why: Not needed: five USE rows are already kept. It is also long, and in Korean 그가 before a relative clause about 누군가 reads awkwardly.
The Korean 그는 그가 … 말했어 is unnatural, but natural Korean (그는 자기가 … or dropping 그가) no longer mirrors fod o one-to-one.
